sources.attributionNote: The OpenNeuro record lists each dataset author with an institutional email address. The names are reproduced; the addresses are not.
sources.privacyReview: Every participant gave written informed consent, and decisional capacity was established, in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki; all research protocols were approved by the University of Iowa Human Subjects Review Board (IRB 201707828). One site, the University of Iowa Movement Disorders Clinic. The recordings are released CC0 by the authors. This is a clinical population, so the publication boundary is tighter than elsewhere on this site: only two model-level scores with descriptive intervals are published. No participant rows, per-person predictions, clinical or cognitive scores, medication state, or per-group age and sex composition — the last of these is in the reviewed inputs and is deliberately left out, because this site does not publish demographic profiles of a diagnosis-specific group. Nothing published here is diagnostic, and no participant can be distinguished in it.

sources.name: OpenNeuro ds004902 · Paired sleep-condition recordings
sources.reason: Downloaded in full and identity-verified, but five FDT payloads in the canonical release are shorter than their own headers and sidecars declare, and all five end inside an incomplete channel frame. The frozen 71-person paired protocol cannot pass its intake gate, so there is no score of any kind. Padding, truncating to the shortest common length, or reporting a partial cohort under the frozen protocol were all refused. What is published is the status and the source-defect counts; no accuracy row exists to publish.
sources.attribution: OpenNeuro ds004902 v1.0.8, cited as the pinned release while this hold stands.
verification: 1,231 files and 8,898,600,609 bytes matched their pinned identities, immutable S3 object versions and git-annex hashes; the defect is therefore upstream, not a failed download.
Both header layouts in the release (77 flat, 141 nested) agree with an independent parser, so the mismatch is not a reader bug.

sources.name: L-FAME · six-person expansion
sources.reason: An audited relative-spectrum description exists for 60 recordings from 6 people, and it is not a model result. Its per-condition numbers are withheld: the descriptors are summarised over 12 recordings per condition from those 6 people, so a minimum or maximum is one person's recording, which this site does not publish. Electrode-row mapping and physical units also remain unresolved, so a spectral profile cannot be read as a biological finding. The published record is the status and the cohort size.
sources.attribution: L-FAME Dataset Benchmark · L-FAME, Hugging Face, at revision 53f4a329eed86a0053b2150cc4e754406662b5a3. Noncommercial scope; attribution required; the source card forbids re-identification attempts.
verification: All 60 raw files rehashed and the descriptors replayed with an independent FFT; the audit's summary hash matches the descriptive summary on this machine.
60 files and 1,170,429,120 bytes matched the pinned Git LFS identities.
The 2026-09-22 two-person descriptors used a different spectral recipe and are not concatenated with this expansion.
